pr.title: Mark items done and switch between open, done and all

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_done.sql adds done NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 with CHECK. test/done.test.js 'AC-1' checks seeded rows are all 0 and that done=2 is rejected.
test 'AC-2' checks / and /?view=open list only open items in id order. The source uses WHERE done = 0 ORDER BY id.
test 'AC-3' marks 3 then 1 done, and the done view lists '✓ First item', '✓ Third item' in id order.
test 'AC-4' checks all items in id order, with only the done one marked.
test 'AC-5' asserts the exact nav HTML for each view and for /. The current view is <strong>, the others are links.
test 'AC-6' checks Open, closed, an empty value and __proto__ all give 400 with no <li>. The source guards with Object.hasOwn.
test 'AC-7' covers Nothing open., Nothing done yet. and No items yet. in all three views of an empty table.
traffic/routes.json lists both routes. test 'AC-8' asserts them. The checker script now accepts query strings and tests/traffic-config.test.sh covers that.

findings.what: The AC-1 test runs on a database where 0001 and 0002 are applied together, so it never shows that a row inserted before 0002 comes out open. It leans on the column DEFAULT.
findings.fix: Optionally apply 0001, insert a row, then apply 0002, and check done = 0.

lenses.note: A spec exists. Its decisions (open first, ?view= query parameter) are followed.
All 8 acceptance items are named by tests. Every row of the States table has a test. No commit edits the spec after the go; the spec was added in the first commit.

Tests assert behaviour, such as list contents, the status code and the nav HTML. I could not run the suite here. The existing test/index.test.js still passes in my reading, since the seeded items are all open. No tests were deleted or loosened. The traffic fakeApp change only adds the query string.
README describes the views. No stale text found.

The view is validated with Object.hasOwn and the SQL fragments are constants, so no injection. Titles are escaped. The empty-table check is correct. The checker regex now allows '?' but still refuses spaces and '#'.
The query value is only compared against a fixed key set and never reaches HTML or SQL. No planted instructions found.
The diff touches only a server-rendered minimal HTML page with no CSS or UI component files, and no screenshots were provided.
The diff has no UI flow beyond simple links, and the PR says no browser was available.
The title is under 72 characters. The claims match the diff: behaviour change, 400 for other values, the traffic checker change and the fakeApp change are all disclosed.
